newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Steel&Tube sees no improvement this year.
newsitem.headline: Steel&Tube sees no improvement this year.

text.p: Steel and Tube Holdings Ltd on Tuesday announced a 23 percent decline in net profit for the 11 months to May 31 and said it did not expect any improvement in trading conditions for the balance of the calendar year.
Steel and Tube posted a NZ$19.6 million profit, $5.7 million less than recorded for the comparable previous period.
"The weaker New Zealand economy led to lower profits earned by the steel distribution sector," Steel and Tube said in a statement.

"The results from the Engineer Group were disappointing in part due to reduced opportunities in the forestry sector. AJ Forsyth & Co, the company's Canadian subsidiary and CP Reinforcing both increased profits in this period."
Steel and Tube declared a taxable bonus issue of one ordinary share for each ordinary share on issue at September 12, 1997.

"For tax purposes the bonus issue will be treated as a dividend in the hands of shareholders at a gross value of $1 per share. Imputation credits of 33 cents per share will attach to each bonus share."
The taxable bonus issue would distribute $14.5 million from the company's imputation credit account.
"Directors expect no improvement in trading conditions for the balance of this calendar year but anticipate some recovery in the first half of 1998," Steel and Tube said.
